steps: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, with the bar on the floor over the middle of your feet. Bend down, keeping your back flat, and grab the bar with an overhand grip (palms facing your body) just outside your legs.
Pull your chest up and tighten your stomach. Start the lift by pushing the floor away with your legs. Keep the bar close to your body as it rises past your knees.

When the bar reaches your upper thighs, drive your hips forward and stand up as fast and as tall as you can, rising up onto your toes, and shrug your shoulders up toward your ears. Your feet may leave the floor slightly, but you're not trying to jump. Then quickly pull your elbows high and out to the sides. As the bar reaches its highest point, drop under it and catch it on the front of your shoulders with your elbows pointing forward. Stand up fully.
Reset your feet. With the bar resting on your shoulders, bend your knees slightly, then straighten them quickly. Use that push to drive the bar upward.
As the bar rises, step one foot forward and the other back into a short, stable stance while you press the bar to arms' length overhead.
Bring your feet back together, one at a time, and hold the bar steady overhead. Then lower the bar to your shoulders and then to the floor, under control.
watchFor: This is one of the most technical lifts in the gym. Learn it with a qualified coach and start with an empty bar, or even a light stick, before adding any weight.
Keep your back flat during the pull. Don't yank with your arms, and don't lean back when catching the bar.
Always practice on a flat, non-slip floor with clear space around you, and know how to let the bar go safely: step away and let it drop. Never try to save a failed lift.

steps: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart with the bar on the floor over the middle of your feet. Bend down, keeping your back flat, and grab the bar with an overhand grip (palms facing your body) just outside your legs.
Pull your chest up and tighten your stomach. Push the floor away with your legs to start the lift, keeping the bar close to your body as it rises past your knees.

When the bar reaches your upper thighs, drive your hips forward and stand up as fast and as tall as you can, rising up onto your toes, and shrug your shoulders up toward your ears. Your feet may leave the floor slightly, but you're not trying to jump. Then quickly pull your elbows high and out to the sides.
Drop your body slightly under the bar and catch it on the front of your shoulders, with your elbows pointing forward and your knees slightly bent.
Stand up fully with the bar resting on your shoulders.
Lower the bar back down in a controlled way, first to your thighs, and then to the floor.
watchFor: This is a technical lift. Learn it with a qualified coach and begin with an empty bar.
Keep your back flat and the bar close to your body. If the bar swings away from you, it's a sign to lower the weight.
Practice on a flat, non-slip floor with clear space. If you miss the catch, step away and let the bar drop. Don't try to catch a bar that is falling.

steps: Take a bar off a rack so it rests on the front of your shoulders, with your elbows pointing forward and your hands just outside your shoulders. Stand with your feet a little wider than hip-width apart.
Keep your chest up and your stomach tight.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower yourself down, as if sitting into a very low chair, keeping your elbows up.
Stand up quickly, pushing through your whole foot.
As you rise, use that momentum to press the bar straight overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders as you sit back down into the next one.
watchFor: Start with an empty bar. This joins a deep knee bend and a press overhead into one fast movement, so it's much harder to control than either part on its own.
Keep your back flat and your knees pointing the same way as your toes.
Don't lean back when the bar goes overhead. If you're out of control, set the bar down and rest.

steps: Stand with your feet a little wider than hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing each other.
Keep your chest up and your stomach tight.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower yourself down, as if sitting into a low chair.
Stand up quickly, pushing through your whole foot, and use that momentum to press the dumbbells straight overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders as you sit back down into the next one.
watchFor: Pick a weight you can press overhead comfortably on its own.
Keep your back flat and your knees pointing the same way as your toes. Don't let your knees cave in.
If you feel your form slip when you're tired, stop and rest.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand, hanging in front of your thighs. Push your hips back and bend your knees slightly, keeping your back flat.
Push your hips forward and stand up quickly, and shrug your shoulders as you pull the dumbbells up close to your body.
Bend your knees slightly and turn your elbows forward so that the dumbbells land at your shoulders, with your palms facing each other.
Straighten your legs and press the dumbbells straight overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders, and then back down to your thighs, under control.
watchFor: Start with light dumbbells to learn the timing.
Keep the dumbbells close to your body when you pull. Don't swing them away from you.
Keep your back flat throughout and don't lean back during the press.

steps: Place a kettlebell on the floor, about a foot in front of you. Stand with your feet a little wider than your shoulders, toes pointing slightly outward. If you only have a dumbbell, hold it upright by one end with both hands.
Push your hips back and bend forward from your hips, keeping your back flat, and grab the handle with both hands.
Tip the kettlebell back and hike it between your legs, like passing a ball backward.
Then push your hips forward hard and stand up tall. That force makes the kettlebell swing forward and up to about chest height. Your arms just guide it and stay straight.
Let the kettlebell fall back down, and as it does, push your hips back so it swings between your legs again.
Keep swinging. Each swing is a powerful push of your hips, not a lift with your arms.
watchFor: The power comes from your hips, not your arms or your back. If your lower back feels strained, stop and check that you're pushing your hips back and forward.
Keep your back flat throughout. Don't round it, even a little, when the weight swings down.
Start with a light weight. Make sure the space in front of you is clear, and don't let go of the weight while it's swinging.

steps: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and put your hands flat on the floor in front of you.
Kick or step your feet back so you're on your hands and toes, with your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest to the floor, then push yourself back up.
Jump or step your feet forward to just outside your hands.
Jump up into the air, reaching your arms overhead. Land softly with your knees slightly bent, and go straight into the next one.
watchFor: Land softly on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent.
Keep your back flat and don't let your hips sag when your feet are back.
You can make it easier by stepping instead of jumping, and by skipping the jump at the end. Move at a pace you can keep up with good form.

steps: Get on your hands and knees on the floor with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Curl your toes under and lift your knees an inch or two off the floor, so your weight is on your hands and toes.
Keep your back flat and your head in line with your spine.
Move one hand and the opposite foot forward at the same time, then the other hand and foot. Keep your knees low and your hips level.
Keep crawling forward, or forward and backward, for the time you've set.
watchFor: Move slowly and stay low, and don't let your hips rise up or sway side to side.
Make sure you have clear floor space in front of you, and wear non-slip shoes or socks.
Keep your wrists flat and directly under your shoulders.

steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand, then place both dumbbells on the floor on either side of you, about shoulder-width apart, with the handles parallel to each other.
Grab the dumbbells and step or jump your feet back so you're on your hands and toes, with your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor and push back up.
Pull one dumbbell up toward your ribs, keeping your body steady, then lower it. Repeat with the other.
Step or jump your feet forward to just outside your hands.
Stand up while pulling the dumbbells up to your shoulders, and then press them overhead until your arms are straight. Lower them and start again.
watchFor: This combines many moves, so use very light dumbbells. Get the sequence right slowly first.
Use dumbbells with flat sides so they don't roll when you rest your weight on them.
Keep your back flat and your wrists steady. Move at a pace you can control.

steps: Anchor the middle of a long, heavy rope to a post, so you have two ends. Stand facing it with your feet a little wider than your shoulders, holding one end in each hand.
Bend your knees slightly and lean forward a little from your hips, with your chest up and your back flat.
Raise and lower your arms in a quick, alternating motion, one after the other, so waves travel down the rope to the post.
Keep your stomach tight and your movements even, and keep going for the time you've set.
watchFor: Keep your back flat and don't let your knees cave in.
Don't hold your breath. Breathe steadily throughout.
Stop and rest if your shoulders start to tighten up. A lighter rope, or smaller waves, will reduce the effort.
